([[Lanham, Maryland]]) | college = *[[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass]] (2022–2023) *[[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] (2023–2025) *[[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] (2026–present) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = | career_end = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2025 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2025]]) * [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]] (2025) * First-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2025) * [[Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] MOP ([[2025 Big East men's basketball tournament|2025]]) * [[Haggerty Award]] (2025) * [[Atlantic 10]] All-Freshman Team (2023) }} '''Reggie Jason Luis Jr.''' (born November 27, 2002) is an American-Dominican [[college basketball]] player for the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]] of the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC). He previously played for the [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass Minutemen]] and [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's Red Storm]]. ==Early life== Luis attended [[Christopher Columbus High School (Miami-Dade County, Florida)|Christopher Columbus High School]] in [[Miami, Florida]], before transferring to Mt. Zion Prep Academy in [[Maryland]]. As a recruit, Luis was rated as the 233rd overall player in the class of 2022 and committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass Minutemen]] under [[Frank Martin (basketball)|Frank Martin]].{{cite web |last=McGavic |first=Matthew |date=April 18, 2023 |title=Report: UMass Transfer R.J. Luis to Visit Louisville |url=https://www.si.com/college/louisville/basketball/rj-luis-to-visit |access-date=March 2, 2025 |publisher=SI.com}} ==College career== === UMass === As a freshman in 2022–23, Luis appeared in 27 games with ten starts, where he averaged 11.5 points, 4.6 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.1 steals per game, while shooting 45.5 percent from the field and 34.8 percent from three-point range. He was named to the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] all-freshman team.{{cite web |last=McGavic |first=Matthew |date=May 7, 2023 |title=Louisville Transfer Target R.J. Luis Commits to St. John's |url=https://www.si.com/college/louisville/basketball/rj-luis-commits |access-date=March 2, 2025 |publisher=SI.com}}{{cite web |last=Braziller |first=Zach |date=May 7, 2023 |title=RJ Luis transferring to St. John's in another big get for Rick Pitino |url=https://nypost.com/2023/05/07/rj-luis-transferring-to-st-johns-in-another-rick-pitino-win/ |access-date=March 2, 2025 |website=The New York Post}} After the season, Luis entered his name into the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{cite web |last=Grabowski |first=Kyle |date=April 4, 2023 |title=UMass basketball freshman guard R.J. Luis enteres [sic] transfer portal |url=https://staging.gazettenet.com/UMass-basketball-freshman-guard-RJ-Luis-enters-transfer-portal-50512011 |access-date=August 8, 2025 |website=Daily Hampshire Gazette}} === St. John's === Luis transferred to play for [[Rick Pitino]] and the [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's Red Storm]].{{cite web |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |date=February 28, 2025 |title=St. John's Pitino says RJ Luis will test NBA Draft waters, is a 'lock' for Big East Player of the Year |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2025/02/rick-pitino-says-rj-luis-will-test-nba-draft-waters-is-a-lock-for-big-east-player-of-the-year.html |access-date=March 2, 2025 |website=NJ.com}} In his first season with the Red Storm in 2023–24, he appeared in just 23 games with ten starts due to being hampered by a hand injury, where he averaged 10.9 points and 4.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last=Sblendorio |first=Peter |date=March 1, 2025 |title=St. John's breakout stars RJ Luis Jr., Zuby Ejiofor Jr. step up in Big East clincher; Aaron Scott leaves with injury |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2025/03/01/st-johns-breakout-stars-rj-luis-jr-zuby-ejiofor-jr-step-up-in-big-east-clincher-aaron-scott-leaves-with-injury/ |access-date=March 2, 2025 |website=New York Daily News}}{{cite web |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |date=July 19, 2024 |title=Rick Pitino expecting 'killer year' from St. John's wing RJ Luis |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2024/07/rick-pitino-expecting-killer-year-from-st-johns-wing-rj-luis.html |access-date=March 2, 2025 |website=NJ.com}} On February 7, 2025, Luis dropped 21 points and seven rebounds in a win over [[2024–25 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]].{{cite web |last=Braziller |first=Zach |date=February 23, 2025 |title=St. John's optimistic RJ Luis Jr. will play vs. rival UConn |url=https://nypost.com/2025/02/23/sports/st-johns-optimistic-rj-luis-jr-will-play-vs-rival-uconn/ |access-date=March 2, 2025 |website=The New York Post}} On February 16, 2025, he notched 21 points, 14 rebounds and five assists in a win over #24 [[2024–25 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]].{{cite web |last=Fox |first=Kyler |date=February 23, 2025 |title=Brooklyn Nets Prospect Watch: RJ Luis Jr.'s Potential |url=https://www.si.com/nba/nets/draft/brooklyn-nets-prospect-watch-rj-luis-jr-potential |access-date=March 2, 2025 |publisher=SI.com}} On March 1, 2025, he scored 21 points and grabbed six rebounds in a win over [[2024–25 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]] to clinch the Big East championship.{{cite web |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |date=March 2, 2025 |title=Seton Hall's Holloway endorses St. John's star for Big East Player of the Year |url=https://www.nj.com/setonhall/2025/03/seton-halls-holloway-endorses-st-johns-star-for-big-east-player-of-the-year.html |access-date=March 2, 2025 |website=NJ.com}}{{cite web |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |date=January 17, 2025 |title=St. John's wing RJ Luis is '100%' going pro after this season, Rick Pitino says |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2025/01/st-johns-wing-rj-luis-is-100-going-pro-after-this-season-rick-pitino-says.html |access-date=March 2, 2025 |website=NJ.com}}{{cite web |last=Braziller |first=Zach |date=February 28, 2025 |title=A 2025-26 St. John's return is still a 'possibility' for star RJ Luis |url=https://nypost.com/2025/02/28/sports/a-2025-26-return-to-st-johns-is-still-a-possibility-for-star-rj-luis/ |access-date=March 2, 2025 |website=The New York Post}} ===LSU=== On May 19, 2026, after a year away from college basketball, Luis signed to play at {{college|LSU}} for head coach [[Will Wade]] after going unselected in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/former-st-john-star-rj-134814165.html|website=[[Yahoo Sports]]|publisher=[[On3.com]]|title=Former St. John’s star RJ Luis signs to play at LSU|date=May 19, 2026|author=Pope, Keegan}} After filing a lawsuit against the NCAA, Luis was granted a preliminary injunction by a judge in [[East Baton Rouge Parish, Louisiana|East Baton Rouge Parish]] District Court and as a result declared eligible for the 2026–27 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.wafb.com/2026/08/25/judge-grants-rj-luis-jr-injunction-clearing-path-play-lsu/|title=Judge grants RJ Luis Jr. injunction, clearing path to play for LSU|author=Tuttle, Ethan|date=August 24, 2026|publisher=[[WAFB]]}} The following day, the [[Southeastern Conference]] ruled him ineligible to play for LSU under its new conference specific rules regarding NBA draft declarations and signed contracts. {{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/49726430/sec-draws-rule-stop-nfl-nba-wnba-players-returning|title=SEC draws rule to stop NFL, NBA, WNBA players from returning|date=August 25, 2026|publisher=[[ESPN.com]]}} ==Professional career== On June 26, 2025 after being undrafted in the [[2025 NBA draft]], Luis signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web |last=Braziller |first=Zach |date=June 27, 2025 |title=Three St. John's stars go pro after signing NBA contracts following draft |url=https://nypost.com/2025/06/27/sports/st-johns-trio-go-pro-after-signing-nba-contracts-after-draft/ |access-date=June 29, 2025 |website=The New York Post}} On August 6, Luis was traded alongside an $8 million trade exception to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Georges Niang]] and two future second-round draft picks.{{Cite web |date=2025-08-06 |title=Celtics Acquire RJ Luis Jr. from Utah Jazz |url=https://celtics.com/news/celtics-acquire-rj-luis-jr-from-utah-jazz |access-date=2025-08-06 |website=celtics.com |language=en}} He was waived on October 15, before the start of the season.{{Cite web |last=Maher |first=Rory |date=October 18, 2025 |title=Celtics' RJ Luis Jr. Chooses His Next Destination: Ron Harper Jr. |url=https://hardwoodhoudini.com/celtics-rj-luis-jr-chooses-his-next-destination-ron-harper-jr |access-date=October 18, 2025 |website=Hardwood Houdini}} Following his cut, Luis signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the Celtics' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Maine Celtics]].{{cite magazine |last=Kirschenbaum |first=Alex |title=Celtics Sign Guard Days After Cutting Him |url=https://www.si.com/nba/celtics/news/celtics-sign-guard-days-after-cutting-him |magazine=Sports Illustrated |publisher=ABG-SI LLC |date=October 18, 2025 |access-date=October 20, 2025 }} Luis was waived by the Maine Celtics before the start of the season due to an injury. ==Personal life== Luis is American, Dominican, and Ecuadorian.{{cite web |title=Reggie Luis (Dominican Republic) - Basketball Stats, Height, Age |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/270501-reggie-luis |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=12 August 2025}}{{cite web |title=.headshot--person_270501--competition_208108 (1200×1625) |url=https://assets.fiba.basketball/image/upload/w_1200,c_fill/q_auto/f_auto/.headshot--person_270501--competition_208108 |access-date=13 September 2025}} Luis' father, Reggie Luis, is Dominican, and his mother, Verito Luis, is Ecuadorian. Luis also has two younger sisters, Racheal and Rylee. He is fluent in both Spanish and English.{{cite web |last=Hagans |first=Keith |title=RJ Luis' mom hits back at fan over 'prima donna' and 'cancer' claims after St. John's exit |url=https://nypost.com/2025/04/03/sports/rj-luis-mom-hits-back-at-fan-over-cancer-claim-after-st-johns-exit/ |website=New York Post |publisher=NYP Holdings Inc. |date=April 3, 2025 |access-date=October 20, 2025}}{{cite web |last=Seidel |first=Scott |title=RJ Luis' Dad Sends Strong Message to Rick Pitino After Son's Career Decision |url=https://athlonsports.com/college-basketball/rj-luis-dad-sends-strong-message-rick-pitino-after-sons-career-decision-nba-draft |website=Athlon Sports |publisher=Athlon Media Group |date=May 28, 2025 |access-date=October 20, 2025 }}{{cite web |title=Who Are RJ Luis Jr.'s Parents?
